item.title: U.S. Senate Democratic candidates to face off in statewide debate
item.description: WGN News will host a debate on February 19 between the leading candidates for the Democratic Party nomination for U.S. Senator from Illinois, moderated by WGN News political editor Tahman Bradley and anchor/reporter Micah Materre.

item.title: 'They messed around, and they found out,' chief says of youths involved in chase
item.description: Peoria police arrested a group of masked individuals after they stole a Jeep and assaulted two juveniles, while also throwing weights and other objects at squad cars and motorists, demonstrating a blatant disregard for human life.

item.title: Peoria judge sentences former tattoo parlor owner for grooming charges
item.description: Mario Davis, 35, was sentenced to four years in prison for grooming a 16-year-old girl after sending her sexually explicit messages on Snapchat, and must register as a sex offender for the next 10 years.

item.title: OSF Healthcare breaks ground on new medical office in Brimfield
item.description: OSF HealthCare leaders broke ground on a new medical office building in Brimfield, which will replace the current clinic and expand access to primary care services, with construction expected to continue through 2026.

item.title: Gov. Pritzker proposes affordable housing, nuclear growth in annual address
item.description: Gov. JB Pritzker gave his eighth state of the state and budget address, proposing a new tax on social media companies, a pause on tax credits for data centers, and legislation to reduce housing costs and junk fees.

item.title: 'It's not cookie cutter': Crittenton Centers staff talk about assistance they provide families
item.description: Crittenton Centers in Peoria offers parenting programs, such as Milestones and Doula, to provide assistance and support for families with their children's milestones.

item.title: Catholics in central Illinois observe Ash Wednesday traditions
item.description: Catholic parishioners in Central Illinois gathered to mark the beginning of Lent, known as "Ash Wednesday," with a mass at Sacred Heart of Jesus Catholic Church in Peoria, where they marked themselves with ashes made from burnt palms from the previous year's Palm Sunday.

item.title: Investigation underway after police vehicle involved in Pekin crash
item.description: A Pekin Police vehicle was involved in a three-vehicle crash on Wednesday, allegedly caused by one of the cars failing to yield to the emergency vehicle, and the incident remains under investigation.

item.title: Fellowship: Soul Food provides nourishment and joy
item.description: Gatherings in the Black community are an important part of the culture, providing a way to connect with one another and pass down traditions, while also providing a source of joy and comfort through soul food, dancing, and games.

item.title: Peoria teens face a bevy of charges related to high speed chase and crash
item.description: Six people, ranging from 13-18 years-old, were charged with robbery, aggravated battery, mob action and other felony counts after leading police on a high-speed chase that included them doing donuts in two high school parking lots and attempting to run a boy over with a stolen Jeep.
